page: Amazon Web Services r7i.metal-24xl is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8488C processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this system features 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz, supported by a 105 MB L3 cache. The server is equipped with 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. It includes no local storage or GPU accelerators, and features a baseline network bandwidth of 38 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core and memory performance. The server achieved a PassMark CPU score of 88,827.32 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 21,623.0, both placing in the top tier. Memory bandwidth tests show strong read-only performance at 7,016.18 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 229.99 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. In database operations, the server processed 104.51 million Redis SET operations per second and scored 31,503.18 in PassMark database operations. Single-core performance is moderate, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2,069.49 and a Geekbench single-core score of 2,186.0, both categorized as average.

The Intel Xeon processor supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512), which accelerate matrix and vector operations. This is reflected in strong LLM inference speeds, processing 294.37 tokens per second for a medium 7B model prompt and 36.8 tokens per second for a large 70B model prompt. Given the high memory density, bare-metal access, and strong multi-threaded capabilities, this server is configured for memory-intensive workloads, large-scale database operations, software compilation, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
